name: Poco
vibe_summary: Poco is a polished, team-oriented OpenClaw alternative built on Claude Code, with a Discord-like server/channel collaboration model and a slick Next.js UI. It emphasizes sandboxed execution, IM integrations, and one-click Docker self-hosting over raw terminal minimalism.

Self-hosters needing IM integration (DingTalk, Feishu, Telegram)

You need a large, mature plugin ecosystem

Native IM integrations and mobile support
openclaw_disadvantages: Smaller community and ecosystem than OpenClaw
Heavier stack (Next.js + FastAPI + Docker) to operate
Tied to Claude Code runtime, less model-agnostic
Younger project with less battle-tested stability

overview_markdown:
Poco positions itself as a safer, more beautiful, and easier-to-use OpenClaw alternative, built around a Claude Code–powered agent core. Its architecture pairs a FastAPI (Python 3.12+) backend with a Next.js 16 frontend, and every task runs inside an isolated container sandbox, with optional local directory mounting for self-hosted deployments. Rather than a single-chat paradigm, Poco organizes work into long-lived servers with channels, DMs, and threads — closer to Discord or Slack — where persistent agents can be mentioned, messages become trackable tasks, and outputs are published as shared files.

Feature-wise it goes well beyond a chatbot: Plan Mode, conversation queueing, project-level defaults for model/preset/Git repo, file uploads, an artifacts viewer (HTML, PDF, Excalidraw, Drawio, and more), and a playback view for replaying command I/O, browser sessions, and MCP tool calls. It supports MCP and Skills for extensibility, a built-in browser for autonomous research, GitHub repo integration, background execution with scheduled triggers, and IM integration via DingTalk, Feishu, and Telegram — plus mobile access and both self-hosted Docker and cloud subscription options.

Compared to OpenClaw, Poco trades terminal-first minimalism and ecosystem depth for a polished, team-oriented product experience with sandboxing on by default. Recent commits show active maintenance — auth redirect fixes, owner-only server deletion, visibility-aware service paths, signed workspace file streaming, and mobile share views — indicating a healthy, fast-moving project, though its younger community and Claude Code dependency are worth weighing.
